- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## Q1 — S3 presign refresh runner

**Component:** `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go` (package `s3presign`)

- Type + constructor: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16` (`type Runner`), `:20` (`NewRunner`)
- **Schedule / interval:** `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`
  ```go
  const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12
  ```
  Ticker created at `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:30` (`ticker := time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)`); loop `:33-40`.
- Work function: `CheckAndPresign` at `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:47`. Pages S3-backed attachments in batches of 100 (`:55`), skips any whose `LastPresignedTime` is under 4 days old (`:85-88`), re-presigns via `s3Client.PresignGetObject` (`:108`), stamps `LastPresignedTime` (`:115`) and updates the attachment `Reference` (`:118`).
- Underlying presign (5-day expiry): `/bench/repo/internal/storage/s3/s3.go:71-84` (expiry comment at `:77`).

**Wiring into startup:**
- Started in `startBackgroundRunners`: `/bench/repo/server/server.go:153` (func), with:
  - `s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)` — `/bench/repo/server/server.go:162`
  - immediate first pass `RunOnce(ctx)` — `/bench/repo/server/server.go:163`
  - **goroutine start of the loop** — `/bench/repo/server/server.go:169` (`s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)`)
- `startBackgroundRunners` is invoked from `Server.Start` at **`/bench/repo/server/server.go:129`**.
- Shutdown path: cancels via `s.backgroundRunnerCancels` — `/bench/repo/server/server.go:157-159`, `:177-183`.
- Read path that consumes the presigned reference: `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:231`.

## Q2 — Outbound webhooks

**(a) Where the HTTP POST executes:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` — `func Post(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) error`
- Request built at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:126`, and the actual network call is **`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`**:
  ```go
  resp, err := safeClient.Do(req)
  ```
- Async fan-out: `PostAsync` at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184` enqueues onto a bounded 128-slot channel (`:39`) drained by 4 worker goroutines started in `init()` at `:42-55`. Queue-full requests are silently dropped with a warning (`:191-195`).
- HMAC (Standard Webhooks) signing: `:133-150`; secret resolution `resolveSigningKey` `:97`; secret generation `GenerateSigningSecret` `:111`.

**(b) SSRF protection — two layers:**

1. **Dial-time guard (the real defense, also defeats DNS rebinding):** the shared client's transport uses `safeDialContext`:
   - Client definition: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37` (`Transport: &http.Transport{DialContext: safeDialContext}`)
   - `safeDialContext`: **`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:59`**, resolves the host at `:65` and rejects any resolved address in a reserved range at `:70-74`.
2. **Admission-time validation on webhook CRUD:** `ValidateURL` at **`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:62`** — scheme must be http/https (`:67`), hostname resolved (`:71`), each IP checked (`:76-81`).
   - Reserved ranges list: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23` (loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.0.0/16 incl. cloud IMDS, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10), parsed once in `init()` `:28-36`.
   - Predicate: `isReservedIP` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:44`.
   - Escape hatch: `AllowPrivateIPs` — `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:41`, short-circuits the check at `:45-47`.

Two things worth flagging:
- `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` is **never set anywhere outside tests** (only refs: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:41,45` and `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook_test.go:90-92,141-143`) — there is no flag/env/profile wiring, so the documented "self-hosted local network" opt-in is currently unreachable in production.
- The reserved list omits `0.0.0.0/8`, `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT), `192.0.0.0/24`, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 (`::ffff:127.0.0.1` parses to an IPv4 that *is* caught by `Contains`, so that one is fine), plus multicast/broadcast.
- `/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/` has **no** equivalent IP guard: `http_getter.go` is a bare `package httpgetter` declaration (1 line), and `util.go` only does media-type parsing. The link-metadata fetch path there is not SSRF-protected by this mechanism.

## Q3 — RPC/gRPC handler methods (question was truncated; answering "which handlers trigger/manage webhooks")

**Handlers that trigger outbound webhook dispatch:**

| RPC handler | path:line | Dispatch call site | Activity type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70` | `:157` `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` | `memos.memo.created` |
| `UpdateMemo` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401` | `:513` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` | `memos.memo.updated` |
| `DeleteMemo` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518` | `:562` `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` | `memos.memo.deleted` |
| `SetMemoRelations` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:16` | `:48` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` | `memos.memo.updated` |
| `SetMemoAttachments` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:16` | `:48` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` | `memos.memo.updated` |
| `CreateMemoComment` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20` | `:119` `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` | `memos.memo.comment.created` |

Dispatch helpers: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:15, 20, 25, 30`, shared impl `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` at `:48`. Shared updated-memo side effect fan-out: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:66`.

**Handlers that manage webhook configuration** (all in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go`):
- `ListUserWebhooks` `:20`
- `CreateUserWebhook` `:53` (validates URL `:74`, generates/validates secret `:82`, `:86`)
- `UpdateUserWebhook` `:106` (validates URL `:161`, `:182`; secret `:170`, `:190`)
- `DeleteUserWebhook` `:205`
- `GetUserWebhookSigningSecret` `:253` (returns the plaintext secret at `:271`; note `ListUserWebhooks`/converters only expose `SigningSecretSet` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:293` and `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:210`)

If Q3 meant something else (e.g. handlers lacking auth checks, or handlers reachable via the Connect router), the registration map is at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go` with ACL config in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` and authz in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/authz.go` — tell me the rest of the question and I'll narrow it.
